walkthrough:
Apply the condition that a quadratic with positive leading coefficient lies entirely above the $x$-axis (no real roots, $b^2 - 4ac < 0$):
$$(-6)^2 - 4(1)(k) < 0 \implies 36 - 4k < 0$$

Equate the curve and the line $y = 7 - 2x$ to form a quadratic equation:
$$x^2 - 6x + k = 7 - 2x \implies x^2 - 4x + (k - 7) = 0$$

Apply the tangency condition of a repeated root, $b^2 - 4ac = 0$:
$$(-4)^2 - 4(1)(k - 7) = 0 \implies 16 - 4k + 28 = 0$$
